clue.text: Crows behind the writer's disturbed rest, taking year to produce book

indicators.note: something disturbed has been moved out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a murder is the collective noun for a flock of crows
the writer's belongs to the setter, so 'my'
taken as written, then rearranged
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Crows squawking behind a writer's house spoil their rest, so a year goes by before the book is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like a verb but is the bird noun: a group of crows is called a murder. The setter's 'my' follows, then the jumbled letters and the year's Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit novel is a kind of book, so the genre name stands for the volume itself.

clue.text: Starter of mayonnaise and stale eggs in European country

indicators.note: a starter comes at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
stale food is old
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A grim menu: mayonnaise and stale eggs served somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a food complaint, but each item is a piece: the sauce's first letter, a synonym for stale, and the scientific word for eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a landlocked nation in eastern Europe lying between Romania and Ukraine.

clue.text: There's a place for cattle in Lutheran Church

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning a word break

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A quaint picture of a church that keeps a spot for cows.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words of the church's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, chiefly in the Americas, where beef cattle are raised and grazed.

clue.text: Catches half-decent hip-hop performances

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of its letters survive, here the back portion

blocks.note: the second three of its six letters
rapping is the vocal style of hip-hop, so its performances are raps

explanation.surface: Someone catches a few hip-hop sets that are only moderately good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' looks like a verb about seeing a show, and it is the definition, in the sense of snaring someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them by trickery, so the plural verb forms match exactly.

clue.text: Maid Marian meets unfortunate town crier's descendents

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters used as written

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's sweetheart bumps into a hapless town crier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meets' looks like the joining verb but is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The town crier once spread public news; established newspapers and broadcasters are the modern successors in that role.

clue.text: Pistol fired, expecting your attention

indicators.note: a fired gun sends things flying, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A gunshot rings out, demanding that everyone look up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' seems to belong with the gun, but it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pampered child always demands notice from others, so the adjective describes that self-centred expectation.

clue.text: Most of lamb the men cooked with cheese

indicators.note: most but not all means the final letter is dropped
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: The men prepare a lamb dish with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen scene is a disguise: the clipped meat and the two words are stirred together.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss holey yellow variety made from cow's milk, one of the best-known examples.

clue.text: Work in the home, coming up with meal: some tongue

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: do-it-yourself, home improvement work
a dish is a prepared meal

explanation.surface: Housework, then a meal, and someone's tongue gets a taste.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY is the British abbreviation for do-it-yourself home repairs. 'Tongue' looks like the meat, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is a language of Ashkenazi Jews, and tongue is a common synonym for language.

clue.text: A Campbell ... and where he might live

blocks.note: first meaning: the American country singer of 'Rhinestone Cowboy' fame
second meaning: a Scottish valley, home ground of the Campbell clan

explanation.walkthrough: Campbell is both the singer's surname and a Scottish clan name, so a clansman would live in a Highland valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Glen Campbell was a famous singer, and a glen is a narrow Scottish valley.

clue.text: Evenly fold material ... becoming this?

indicators.note: even means the second, fourth and so on, so only those positions are kept
becoming means turning into something else, so the letters change their arrangement

blocks.note: its second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Folding cloth neatly so it turns into a bespoke garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: cloth folded with care ends up made to measure, and the letters likewise reshape into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth that is cut and folded neatly by a tailor ends up as a garment fitted to its owner.

clue.text: Rib leading to human, oddly; ousted in Bible book

indicators.note: the odd positions are thrown out, leaving the even ones behind

blocks.note: to rib someone is to tease or josh them
second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Recalls Eve made from Adam's rib, a human expelled from Eden in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' points to Genesis but is a verb meaning tease. 'Oddly; ousted' means the odd letters go, not that they stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is the sixth book of the Old Testament, following Deuteronomy.

clue.text: Harshly disciplined, ignoring corrupt ICI? Excellent!

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so those letters are removed
corrupted means altered from the proper form, so the letters to remove need not appear in the given order
treated harshly suggests being knocked about, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the chemical company's initials, used as letters to strike out

explanation.surface: A company boss praises staff who were strictly punished, without the crooked chemical giant ICI.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British firm. Its three letters are taken out of the long word, in any order, and the rest rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are exclamations of approval meaning very good or first-rate.

clue.text: Friend, not at home among clerical profession, finding form of divination

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters it governs are taken out of a longer word

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
the ministry is the profession of clergy
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A friend who isn't at home, mixing with clergy, discovers a way of telling the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' is the common crossword IN; it is cut from the middle of the clergy's calling.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the lines of a hand to foretell the future is a recognised kind of fortune-telling practice.

clue.text: When embracing a king, Everyman's reportedly gnawed on a royal personage

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece wraps around another
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, speaking of his own
taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king
chewed her, said casually, dropping the h

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to having bitten a queen while hugging a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyman's' is the setter's own name, so it gives the possessive 'my'. The second word comes from 'chewed 'er' spoken with a dropped h.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary I of England, daughter of Henry VIII, reigned from 1553 to 1558 as queen.

clue.text: Head of state (& historically, Arabic honcho)?

definitions.text: Head of state (& historically, Arabic honcho)?

indicators.note: the head is the top or front, so each word gives only its first letter

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A definition of an old Middle Eastern ruler, with an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' applies to every word after it, taking the initials. Read whole, the clue also describes the ruler, though strictly a shah was Persian, not Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was used by monarchs of Iran until 1979, making them historical heads of state.

clue.text: For you and me, time's called

indicators.note: called out means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: hours measure time; with the h silent it matches

explanation.surface: A pub landlord calling time, telling the two of us the last round is ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's called' looks like the British pub cry at closing, but time is hours, and the h drops away when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to both speaker and listener, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Drunken Milo embraces mate (it's a tree)

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order
to embrace is to hug, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: the name taken as letters
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: Tipsy Milo hugs his friend, and a bracket explains he is actually a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged name opens to let the friend in, between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This African tropical tree is grown for the oil pressed from its fruit, so it is a particular species.

clue.text: Lost, alone, after pub crawl's initiation in the City

indicators.note: an initiation is a beginning, so only the first letter is kept
something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander out of order
after places the scrambled piece behind the others in the sequence

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ends up lost and alone in town after starting a pub crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost, alone' reads as the person's plight, but it gives the scrambled ending. A pub crawl is a night going from bar to bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan capital is a major Spanish port, so a definite reference to a particular big city fits.

clue.text: Red couch I 'antiqued' to some extent

indicators.note: only partly, so the letters are a portion sitting inside the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the pronoun, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone admits to having distressed a red sofa to look old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like the couch's colour but is a noun, a red wine, as in a glass of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan wine, nearly always red, so it is one example of a red.

clue.text: Kind of sole you shouldn't find on a slipper?

definitions.text: Kind of sole you shouldn't find on a slipper?

blocks.clueFragment: Kind of sole you shouldn't find on a slipper?
blocks.note: surface reading: a sole not usually fitted to bedroom footwear
setter's reading: a slipper is anything that slips, so a grippy sole is the opposite of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipper' is the house shoe on the surface, but read as one who slips, a grippy, anti-sliding sole would be a contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sole designed to grip and stop sliding describes footwear tread built to prevent slips.

clue.text: Half of spuds hidden by second-hand agricultural compound

indicators.note: half means only part survives, so the back portion is dropped
in a down entry one piece is screened from view by what comes next, so they sit one after the other

blocks.note: spuds are potatoes; the first four of its eight letters
S is the abbreviation for second
H is the abbreviation for hand

explanation.surface: A farmer hides some potatoes behind a used fertiliser sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-hand' reads as used, but splits into two abbreviations. Spud is informal for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium salt widely spread on fields as fertiliser, hence its farming use.

clue.text: Another way to see romp around sordid flat? Windows, perhaps

indicators.note: viewing it another way means rearranging it into a different form
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
sordid suggests something messy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sleazy flat where a romp went on, seen through its windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like part of the flat, but it is Microsoft's operating system; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing, an operating system such as Windows is the base on which software runs.

clue.text: I regularly told fiancée to obtain antiseptic

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps telling their fiancée to pick up something for a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I regularly told' reads as a habit, but 'regularly' acts on the words after it, not on the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture of the element is applied to wounds to kill germs, so it serves as a disinfectant.

clue.text: Old boy with gossip about 'remarkable elephant'

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
mud is scandalous talk, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: An old man spreading rumours about an extraordinary elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but signals the turnaround of both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's baby elephant could fly using his huge ears, a truly unusual creature.

clue.text: Clothes shop helper not, on the face of it, a kind of servant

indicators.note: the face is the front, so only the leading letter is kept

blocks.note: H&M, the high-street fashion chain, with the ampersand spelt out
an aide is an assistant
first letter

explanation.surface: A shop assistant in a clothes store who is not, outwardly, a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes shop helper' wants to be one phrase meaning a sales assistant; it splits into the retailer H&M, read as H AND M, and a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaiden is a female personal attendant, a particular type of domestic servant.

clue.text: Speaker's helper to be found before November

blocks.note: first meaning: a microphone helps a speaker be heard
second meaning: the NATO alphabet code word for M, which precedes N

explanation.walkthrough: 'November' looks like the month, but it is the radio code word for N, and M's code word comes just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form of microphone, and the NATO phonetic name for the letter preceding N.

clue.text: 'Milord? Graham's performing something in the bog'

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act or a transformation, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A servant tells his lordship that Graham is busy in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for a toilet, which the surface plays on; the definition means a real bog, a wet marshy area.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant grows in wetlands, so it is one thing found in boggy ground.
